overview: 96 official Qs (2008, 2017, 2019, 2025). Parliament (33) and the Union/State executive (27) dominate; legislatures/Legislative Councils and the judiciary give 13 each; judicial review and activism are small (8 together). Mostly one-liners on 'who presides / who decides / how many / which Article', plus many 'all correct except' stems (2017) and statement-based multi-picks (2025).

possibility.evidence: 0 official Qs on the umbrella leaf
possibility.what_they_ask: natural targets judged from neighbours: Part V (Union) vs Part VI (States) article ranges, separation of powers between the three organs, Art 50, Art 77 (business in the President's name).

possibility.angle: Legislative, executive, judiciary – AP-specific and organ roles
possibility.what_they_ask: Anglo-Indian nomination (President 2 / Governor 1, ended 2020); AP–Telangana Rajya Sabha split (11/7).

Art 169 procedure; Council composition fractions; money bill delay (14 days); number of bicameral States (time-sensitive); AP Council abolition 1985/revival 2007; fate of Council-originated bills; Rajya Sabha permanence.

possibility.angle: Executive: President, Vice-President, Council of Ministers, Governor, AG
possibility.what_they_ask: electoral college of President vs VP; removal of VP (Rajya Sabha first); pardon (Art 72 vs 161); ordinance life (6 months 6 weeks); 15% cap / minimum 12 (91st Amd); Art 75(5) six months; AG tenure and remuneration; Part V.

possibility.angle: Parliament: officers, sessions, bills, committees, financial procedure
possibility.what_they_ask: who presides joint sitting; Speaker's money-bill certificate; prorogation vs recess; Art 85 gap; PAC/CoPU/Estimates roles; charged expenditure; seat counts per State; Zero Hour; no-confidence; privileges.

Art 124 (Parliament fixes SC strength); collegium origin (judgments); NJAC/99th Amd struck down 2015; Art 128 / 224A retired judges with President's consent; Art 233 district judges; HC age 62; advisory jurisdiction Art 143.
article through which exercised (32, with 13; 226 for HCs); judicial review as feature of federalism; legislature's response to a judgment (validating law / amendment).

PIL pioneers (Bhagwati, Krishna Iyer); PIL = Social Action Litigation = activism (not restraint); judge-made doctrines vs constitutional text; landmark directions (Seema v Ashwani Kumar – marriage registration); US origin of the concept.

traps.trap: Gives a Lok Sabha power to the Rajya Sabha [or vice versa]
traps.spot: Options 'Lok Sabha / Rajya Sabha / either House / joint sitting'
traps.fix: Collective responsibility → Lok Sabha only (Art 75(3)); VP removal resolution → only Rajya Sabha first (Art 67(b)); money bills → only Lok Sabha.
traps.pyq: 'Council of Ministers collectively responsible to' → The Lok Sabha [prelims-2017#55]; VP removal moved first only in → The Rajya Sabha [prelims-2019#62]

traps.trap: Adds nominated members to the President's electoral college
traps.spot: Multi-select of elected/nominated members of Parliament and Assemblies
traps.fix: President (Art 54): only ELECTED MPs and ELECTED MLAs incl. Delhi and Puducherry. VP (Art 66): ALL MPs, elected and nominated, no MLAs. MLCs vote for neither.
traps.pyq: Electoral college → A, C and E (nominated members out) [mains-2025-paper1#119]; CM who is an MLC cannot vote [mains-2017-paper2#139]

traps.trap: Swaps the authority under whose pleasure / by whose determination an office is held
traps.spot: Statements on AG, Advocate General, ministers naming PM, Parliament or Governor
traps.fix: AG – pleasure of the President and remuneration fixed by the President (Art 76); Advocate General – Governor (Art 165); Union ministers – President's pleasure (Art 75(2)).
traps.pyq: 'AG holds office during pleasure of the Prime Minister' and 'remuneration as Parliament may determine' → both false [mains-2025-paper1#124]; Advocate General's pay → as determined by the Governor [prelims-2017#61]

traps.trap: Changes the fractions or numbers in a composition
traps.spot: Fractions 1/3, 1/12, 1/6 or counts (2 vs 1 nominees, 20/10 members)
traps.fix: Council: 1/3 local bodies, 1/12 graduates, 1/12 teachers, 1/3 MLAs, 1/6 nominated. Anglo-Indian: President 2 (LS), Governor 1 (Assembly).
traps.pyq: '1/13 elected by Legislative Assembly' is the false one (it is 1/3) [mains-2017-paper2#119]; Governor nominating 2 Anglo-Indians → false, only 1 [prelims-2019#61]

traps.trap: Gives the President a power over money bills he does not have
traps.fix: Art 111 proviso: the President may assent or withhold, but cannot return a money bill; Speaker's certificate is final (Art 110(3)).
traps.pyq: 'President may return money bill for reconsideration' → the incorrect statement [mains-2017-paper2#77]; final say on money bill → Speaker [prelims-2017#57]

traps.trap: Moves pardon or death-sentence powers between President and Governor
traps.fix: Only the President pardons a death sentence and courts-martial sentences; the Governor may suspend, remit or commute a death sentence.
traps.pyq: 'The only authority for pardoning a sentence of death is the President' → correct [mains-2017-paper2#90]

traps.fix: PIL (Social Action Litigation) grew from judicial activism – relaxed locus standi, epistolary jurisdiction.
traps.pyq: 'PIL is an outcome of Judicial Restraint' → false [mains-2025-paper1#115]

traps.trap: Confuses which expenditure is charged on which Consolidated Fund
traps.spot: 'Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, except'
traps.fix: CFI: debt charges, SC judges' salaries and pensions, HC judges' pensions. Governors' emoluments → State Consolidated Fund (HC judges' salaries too).
traps.pyq: 'Pensions of governors of any state' → not charged on CFI [mains-2017-paper2#76]

techniques.name: Who-decides map [office → authority]
techniques.how: For any 'who presides / who decides / whose consent' stem, recall the single constitutional authority named in the Article; options naming a political body (party, cabinet, PM) usually fall when the text names an office.
techniques.example: Art 224A retired HC judge – the text says 'previous consent of the President' → Governor, Parliament, CJI fall → The President [mains-2017-paper1#99]

techniques.name: Time-limit ladder
techniques.how: Keep one ladder: 14 days (Council on money bill, RS on money bill), 6 weeks (ordinance after reassembly), 6 months (non-MP minister; gap between sessions), 5 years (President, VP). Match the number to the institution.
techniques.example: Ordinance lasts 6 weeks after Parliament reassembles, and the gap cannot exceed 6 months → 6 months 6 weeks [mains-2017-paper2#111]

techniques.name: Executive vs legislative tool sort
techniques.how: Classify each option by who wields it: the House (questions, resolutions, motions, committees) or the executive (dissolution, ordinances). The odd one out answers 'not a tool of legislative control'.
techniques.example: Questions, resolution, no-confidence are House tools; dissolution is the President's on PM's advice → Dissolution of the House [mains-2017-paper2#148]

techniques.name: Text vs judge-made test
techniques.how: Ask: is this written in the Constitution or did a judgment create it? Collegium, basic structure, PIL, handcuff limits are judge-made; exemptions to FRs, joint sitting are text.
techniques.example: Collegium is not in Art 124 → it arises from the Second and Third Judges cases → Decisions of Supreme Court [prelims-2017#58]; 'Exemptions to Fundamental Rights' is constitutional text → not the SC's evolution [mains-2017-paper2#105]

techniques.name: Time-stamp the question
techniques.how: For counts and office-holders, note the exam year and answer for that date (bicameral States, Anglo-Indian seats, presiding officers).
techniques.example: In 2017 seven States had Councils incl. J&K → 7 (six after Oct 2019) [mains-2017-paper2#83]

confusions.remember: Adjournment suspends a sitting; prorogation ends the session (bills survive, motions/notices lapse); recess = gap between prorogation and new session.
Dissolution ends the House – bills pending in LS lapse; prorogation does not kill bills.
President: elected MPs + elected MLAs; VP: all MPs only.
Only 72 covers death-sentence pardon and courts-martial.
AG = first law officer, constitutional, President's pleasure; SG statutory; Advocate General = State, Governor's pleasure.
PAC = watchdog on expenditure via CAG reports, opposition chair by convention; Estimates = economy in estimates; CoPU = PSUs (Krishna Menon, 1964).
Question Hour = admitted questions with notice; Zero Hour = any urgent matter, no notice, Indian innovation.
Parliament by law raises SC judges; the President fixes HC strength.
Both need the President's previous consent; 128 requested by CJI, 224A by HC Chief Justice.
Minimum 12 applies only to States (91st Amd 2003).
168 lists legislatures; 169 creation/abolition of Councils (special-majority resolution + Act of Parliament); 171 composition.
RS permanent: one-third retire every second year; LS 5 years unless dissolved.
Mavalankar first Speaker; Ananthasayanam Ayyangar first Deputy Speaker, Speaker from 1956.

anchors: Art 54/55 President's election; Art 56 term 5 years; Art 57 re-election unlimited
Art 64 VP ex-officio Chairman RS; Art 66 election; Art 67(b) removal via RS
Art 75(2) pleasure of President; 75(3) collective responsibility to LS; 75(5) six months
Art 76 Attorney General – qualified as SC judge, audience in all courts
Art 77 all executive action in the name of the President
Art 85 – not more than 6 months between last sitting and first sitting of next session
Art 110(3) Speaker certifies money bill; Art 111 President cannot return it
Art 118(4) – Speaker presides over joint sitting
Art 123 ordinance: 6 weeks after reassembly (max 6 months 6 weeks)
Art 169 Councils; Art 198 – 14 days for money bills
99th Amd / NJAC struck down 16 Oct 2015 (Chelameswar dissent)
Art 217 – HC judge to 62; Art 233 – district judges by Governor with HC
Lok Sabha seats: UP 80, Maharashtra 48, WB 42; Meghalaya 2
AP Council: abolished 1985, revived 2007; AP Rajya Sabha 11, Telangana 7
checklist: Which office or House does the Article name – not who acts in practice?
Elected only, or elected and nominated?
Match the number to its institution on the time-limit ladder (14 days / 6 weeks / 6 months).
Negative stem: mark each option T/F; the false one usually moves a power to the wrong authority.
Is the feature in the constitutional text or judge-made?
Count-type questions: answer for the exam year.
